indian_states: Pan-India (Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh)

leaf_characteristics.shape: Simple, ovate to broadly lanceolate glossy dark green leaves with distinct serrate margins

stem_characteristics: Multi-stemmed woody erect branching evergreen shrub, 1.5–4.0 m
flower_characteristics: Large, showy solitary funnel-shaped 5-petaled flowers (crimson, red, yellow, pink) with long protruding staminal column
fruit_characteristics: Rarely sets capsule under cultivation in India
growth_habit: Vigorous bushy evergreen woody ornamental and medicinal shrub, 1.5–4.0 meters
habitat_and_climate: Warm tropical and sub-tropical climate; completely frost-tender
water_requirements: Regular moderate watering; keep moist but well-drained
soil_preferences: Fertile, rich, well-drained loamy soil rich in organic compost, pH 6.0–7.0
propagation_methods: Semi-hardwood stem cuttings or air layering
uses: Revered sacred flower offered to deities (Goddess Kali, Lord Ganesha)
Traditional hair care: petals and leaves crushed into natural conditioning shampoo and hair growth oil
Hibiscus sour tea rich in Vitamin C and anthocyanins
safety_notes: Safe for topical and dietary culinary use.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Mealybug (Ferrisia virgata)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: White waxy clusters on flower buds and leaf axils causing bud drop
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Spray Neem oil (5 ml/L) + liquid soap or Imidacloprid

prevention_guidance: Prune in early spring to stimulate vigorous new flowering shoots
Spray iron chelate if interveinal yellowing (chlorosis) appears

leaf_characteristics.shape: Simple, broadly ovate to elliptic glossy dark green opposite leaves with prominent veins

stem_characteristics: Erect or scrambling woody perennial shrub or twining climber, 1–3 m
flower_characteristics: Intensely fragrant solitary or clustered pure white waxy flowers opening at dusk (single or multi-whorled double petals)
fruit_characteristics: Small globose purple-black berry (rarely produces seeds under cultivation)
growth_habit: Dense bushy evergreen woody shrub or scrambling climber, 1–3 meters
habitat_and_climate: Warm tropical and sub-tropical plains; flourishes in hot sunny summers
water_requirements: Regular moderate watering; withstands brief drying
soil_preferences: Well-drained rich sandy loam to clay loam rich in organic manure, pH 6.5–7.5
propagation_methods: Semi-hardwood stem cuttings or ground layering
uses: World-renowned aromatic floral crop: Madurai Malli garland flowers for temple rituals and weddings
Mogra attar and perfume extraction, jasmine green tea
Aromatherapy for relaxation and stress relief
safety_notes: Safe and celebrated in traditional culture.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Bud Worm (Hendecasis duplifascialis)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Caterpillar bores inside unopened white flower buds causing reddish-brown discoloration and bud drop
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Foliar spray of Spinosad 45 SC (0.3 ml/L) or Neem oil

prevention_guidance: Annual pruning to 45 cm height in November–December is mandatory for profuse summer flowering flushes

leaf_characteristics.shape: Odd-pinnate compound leaves with 3–7 ovate serrate leaflets and spiny glandular petioles
leaf_characteristics.color: Rich dark green with reddish flush on young growth

stem_characteristics: Woody, prickly erect or scrambling shrub with curved prickles (thorns) on green stems, 1–2.5 m
flower_characteristics: Exquisitely fragrant solitary or clustered multi-petaled flowers (pink, red, white, yellow) with numerous stamens
fruit_characteristics: Fleshy red to orange globose hypanthium (rose hip) holding achene seeds
growth_habit: Prickly deciduous or semi-evergreen woody perennial shrub, 1–2.5 meters
habitat_and_climate: Mild temperate to subtropical climate; requires warm sunny days and cool nights for maximum fragrance
water_requirements: Regular moderate watering; keep root zone moist but never waterlogged
soil_preferences: Deep, rich, well-drained fertile loamy soil high in organic humus, pH 6.0–6.8
growing_season: Winter and Spring peak blooming (Desi Gulab, Damask Rose, Hybrid Teas)
propagation_methods: T-budding on Rosa multiflora rootstock or hardwood cuttings
uses: Desi Gulab / Damask Rose for Kannauj rose water (gulab jal) and pure rose attar
Sweet gulkand (rose petal preserve) for cooling Ayurvedic health
Commercial cut flower bouquets and garlands
safety_notes: Stems have sharp prickles (thorns). Wear protective gloves.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Black Spot (Diplocarpon rosae)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Fringed circular black spots on leaves leading to severe yellowing and premature leaf drop
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Foliar spray of Mancozeb (2 g/L) or Trifloxystrobin; water at base, not on leaves

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Powdery Mildew (Podosphaera pannosa)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: White talc-like powdery fungal growth on young leaves, buds, and stems causing distortion
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Spray Wettable Sulfur (2 g/L) or Hexaconazole

prevention_guidance: Annual pruning in October (cut back to 40 cm with angled cuts) stimulates vigorous winter blooming
Apply mustard oil cake and bone meal around root basin

leaf_characteristics.shape: Pinnately divided feathery aromatic leaves with narrow lanceolate serrate segments dotted with oil glands
leaf_characteristics.color: Dark green with pungent distinctive aroma

stem_characteristics: Erect, grooved herbaceous branching stem with strong aromatic scent, 30–100 cm
flower_characteristics: Large, dense, globose composite flower heads (capitulum) packed with bright orange or yellow ray florets
fruit_characteristics: Slender, compressed black cypsela (achene) topped by pappus bristles
growth_habit: Erect bushy annual herbaceous flowering plant, 30–100 cm
habitat_and_climate: Warm sub-tropical and tropical climate; performs outstandingly in bright dry sunny weather
water_requirements: Moderate regular watering; avoids wet soggy soil
soil_preferences: Well-drained fertile sandy loam to clay loam rich in organic matter, pH 6.5–7.5
growing_season: All three seasons (Kharif, Winter, and Summer for festive demand)
propagation_methods: Certified seed sowing or terminal cuttings
uses: Major commercial garland flower for Diwali, Dussehra, pujas, weddings
Rich source of natural lutein pigment used in eye health supplements and poultry feed
Potent nematicidal root exudates (alpha-terthienyl) suppress root-knot nematodes in soil

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Leaf Spot / Blight (Alternaria tagetica)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Circular brownish-black necrotic spots on leaves and flower ray florets
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Foliar spray of Mancozeb (2 g/L)

prevention_guidance: Plant as companion trap crop around tomato, brinjal, and chilli borders to eliminate parasitic nematodes
Pinch terminal growing tip at 30 days to stimulate 15–20 productive lateral branches

indian_states: Pan-India (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal)

leaf_characteristics.shape: Simple, opposite, elliptic-obovate glossy dark green leaves with pale midrib and milky sap

stem_characteristics: Erect herbaceous to semi-woody branched subshrub with smooth green or purplish stems, 30–90 cm
flower_characteristics: Salverform 5-lobed flat flowers, pure white or vivid rosy-pink with dark reddish-purple eye
fruit_characteristics: Paired cylindrical dehiscent follicles (2–4 cm) holding small black grooved seeds
growth_habit: Hardy erect bushy perennial subshrub, 30–90 cm
habitat_and_climate: Tropical and sub-tropical semi-arid climate; extraordinary drought and heat tolerance
sunlight_requirements: Full blazing sun to light shade
soil_preferences: Thrives in poor, sandy, gravelly, rocky, and saline soils, pH 6.0–8.0
uses: Commercial source of life-saving vinca alkaloids (vincristine and vinblastine used in chemotherapy for leukemia and Hodgkin's lymphoma)
Ayurvedic remedies for type 2 diabetes and hypertension
Hardy ornamental border plant
safety_notes: CRITICAL TOXICITY WARNING: Contains over 130 powerful cytotoxic indole alkaloids. Plant is poisonous if ingested in unprescribed quantities. Keep away from pets and small children.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Die-back / Twig Blight (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Drying of upper twigs during heavy monsoon
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Ensure good drainage; spray Copper Oxychloride

prevention_guidance: Thrives in neglected sunny dry gardens with near-zero maintenance
